meanings: contrary to what one might expect

components.note: 亻 (person) — 倒 relates to a person falling over
到 (dào) gives the sound — 倒 is also pronounced dào, an exact match
Traditionally analyzed as 日 combined with 疋, linked to the idea of speaking directly and truthfully — the source of 是's meaning 'to be, indeed, right.'

example.hanzi: 他倒是很喜欢这个主意。
example.pinyin: Tā dàoshi hěn xǐhuan zhè ge zhǔyi.
example.english: He actually quite likes this idea, surprisingly.
example.fact: Velcro was invented in 1941 after Swiss engineer George de Mestral noticed how burdock seed burrs clung to his dog's fur and his own clothing during a walk in the Alps — an accidental observation that led to one of the most widely used fasteners in the world.

components.note: 手 (hand) — depicts a hand raised above the eyes.
目 (eye) — shielding the eyes with a hand to look into the distance gave 看 its meaning 'to look, to see.'
彳 (a road/step) — someone arriving on the road
寺 (a court/hall) — the destination where the visitor is welcomed

example.hanzi: 我们应该客观地看待这个问题。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi kèguān de kàndài zhège wèntí.
example.english: We should look at this problem objectively.
example.fact: The checker shadow illusion, created by MIT vision scientist Edward Adelson in 1995, shows two identically colored gray squares that appear to be starkly different shades because of a shadow cast across the checkerboard pattern — a vivid demonstration of how the brain's brightness perception depends heavily on surrounding context.

components.note: 阝 (hill) — 降 originally related to coming down a hill or slope
夅 (jiàng) gives the sound — an exact match with 降's reading jiàng
氐 (dī) gives the sound — 低 is also pronounced dī, an exact match

example.hanzi: 这项新政策有助于降低碳排放。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng xīn zhèngcè yǒuzhù yú jiàngdī tàn páifàng.
example.english: This new policy helps reduce carbon emissions.
example.fact: In 1987, the Montreal Protocol became the first international treaty ratified by every country on Earth, phasing out ozone-depleting chemicals like CFCs; the resulting recovery of the ozone layer is expected to be complete by around 2066, and the treaty is often cited as the most successful environmental agreement in history.

components.note: 艹 (grass/plant) — the grass/plant radical, marking the character as related to plants or vegetation.
署 (shǔ) gives the sound — an exact match with 薯's reading.
木 (tree) at the base of the character — 条 originally named a slender branch or twig, later extended to 'strip, item, article.'

example.hanzi: 孩子们最爱吃薯条了。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zuì ài chī shǔtiáo le.
example.english: Kids love french fries the most.
example.fact: The potato was first domesticated by indigenous peoples in the Andes mountains of present-day Peru and Bolivia more than 7,000 years ago, and Spanish conquistadors carried it back to Europe in the 16th century, where it eventually became a staple crop credited with helping fuel population growth across the continent.

components.note: 足 (foot) — relates to 路's meaning 'road, path,' something walked on with feet.
各 (gè) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from lù.
辶 (walking/movement) — links 边's meaning to a boundary or edge one moves along.
臱 (biān) gives the sound — 边 is also pronounced biān, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 我们在路边等出租车。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài lùbiān děng chūzūchē.
example.english: We waited for a taxi on the roadside.
example.fact: The Roman road network, built up over centuries starting around 312 BC with the Via Appia, eventually spanned more than 400,000 kilometers connecting the empire, and its durable multi-layered construction technique kept some sections in use for more than a thousand years.

components.note: 毛 (fur/hair) — 毯 names a woven covering made from fur or wool.
炎 (yán) gives a sound distantly related to tǎn, having drifted apart over time.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 晚上很冷,我盖了两条毯子。
example.pinyin: Wǎnshang hěn lěng, wǒ gài le liǎng tiáo tǎnzi.
example.english: It was very cold at night, so I covered myself with two blankets.
example.fact: Merino sheep, originally bred in Spain and later refined into a distinct breed in Australia during the 18th and 19th centuries, produce some of the finest and softest wool in the world, prized for insulating fibers that can be several times thinner than a human hair.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 惊 relates to an emotional reaction of shock or fright
京 (jīng) gives the sound — an exact match with 惊's reading jīng
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a rider.
可 here is said to depict a mount — a person riding in an unusual way gave 奇 its meaning 'strange, odd, remarkable.'

example.hanzi: 大家对这个发现感到十分惊奇。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā duì zhège fāxiàn gǎndào shífēn jīngqí.
example.english: Everyone was greatly amazed by this discovery.
example.fact: When archaeologist Howard Carter opened the tomb of the Egyptian pharaoh Tutankhamun in 1922, he found over 5,000 artifacts virtually undisturbed after more than 3,000 years, including the boy king's iconic solid-gold burial mask — one of the most complete royal tombs ever discovered in the Valley of the Kings.

components.note: 车 (cart) — 输 originally meant to transport goods by cart.
俞 (yú) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading shū has diverged.
入 depicts a simple wedge or arrow shape pointing inward, showing the direction of entering.

example.hanzi: 请在这里输入你的密码。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ shūrù nǐ de mìmǎ.
example.english: Please enter your password here.
example.fact: The QWERTY keyboard layout, patented by Christopher Latham Sholes in 1878 for early typewriters, was arranged partly to reduce mechanical jams by separating commonly paired letters — and despite more efficient layouts being proposed since, it remains the dominant standard for keyboards worldwide.

components.note: 止 (a foot) — represents forward motion.
舟 (a boat) — a foot boarding a boat moving ahead gave 前 its meaning 'front, forward, before.'
大 (a grown man) — the figure being depicted.
一 (a hairpin) — worn across the top of the head to mark a coming-of-age ceremony, giving 夫 its meaning 'man, husband.'

example.hanzi: 她和前夫依然保持着朋友关系。
example.pinyin: Tā hé qiánfū yīrán bǎochí zhe péngyou guānxi.
example.english: She and her ex-husband still remain friends.
example.fact: Ancient Rome allowed divorce by mutual consent as early as the 3rd century BC, making it markedly more permissive than many societies that followed; a Roman marriage could be legally ended simply by one party declaring intent in front of witnesses, without requiring court approval.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — throwing is an action done with the hand.
乃 (nǎi) gives a sound distantly related to rēng, having drifted apart over time.
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.

example.hanzi: 他把书包扔下就跑出去了。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ shūbāo rēngxià jiù pǎo chūqu le.
example.english: He threw down his backpack and ran outside.
example.fact: The discus throw was one of the original events at the ancient Olympic Games in Greece, dating back to at least the 5th century BC, and is famously depicted in the sculpture Discobolus — a bronze original later lost, known today only through Roman marble copies.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 管 originally referred to a bamboo pipe or tube, later broadening to mean 'to manage' or 'to control.'
官 (guān) gives a hint of the sound — 管 is pronounced guǎn, a connection that has shifted only slightly in tone.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 水从这根管子流出来。
example.pinyin: Shuǐ cóng zhè gēn guǎnzi liú chūlái.
example.english: Water flows out from this pipe.
example.fact: The Romans built an extensive network of aqueducts starting around 312 BC, some stretching more than 80 kilometers, using precisely calculated gradients to move water entirely by gravity — the Pont du Gard in France, still standing after nearly 2,000 years, was once part of a 50-kilometer system supplying the city of Nîmes.

meanings: fig. to appear on the scene
used in advertising to mean new product

components.note: 癶 (two feet) — 登 relates to climbing or ascending with one's legs
豆 (dòu) gives a sound distantly related to 登's reading dēng, having drifted apart over time
土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 新一代的电动汽车即将登场。
example.pinyin: Xīn yī dài de diàndòng qìchē jíjiāng dēngchǎng.
example.english: The new generation of electric cars is about to make its debut.
example.fact: The first practical electric car predates the gasoline-powered automobile: inventors in the 1880s and 1890s, including Britain's Thomas Parker, built working electric vehicles, and by 1900 roughly a third of all cars in the United States were electric, before cheap gasoline and mass production shifted the market.

components.note: A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
木 (wood) — 格 originally meant a wooden branch or standard, extended to 'pattern, style, rule.'
各 (gè) gives a sound hint — 格 is pronounced gé, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 他的人格深受周围人的尊重。
example.pinyin: Tā de réngé shēn shòu zhōuwéi rén de zūnzhòng.
example.english: His character is deeply respected by those around him.
example.fact: The 'Big Five' personality model — openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism — emerged from decades of statistical analysis of trait-descriptive language starting in the 1980s, and remains one of the most replicated frameworks in psychology for describing how people differ from one another.

meanings: to win (a set, a game etc)

components.note: 手 (hand) — 拿 means to take or hold something in the hand
合 (hé) gives a sound related to 拿's reading ná, from an older, closer pronunciation link
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.

example.hanzi: 中国队最终拿下了这场比赛的冠军。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó duì zuìzhōng náxià le zhè chǎng bǐsài de guànjūn.
example.english: The Chinese team ultimately won the championship of this match.
example.fact: In 2004, the Boston Red Sox became the first team in Major League Baseball history to win a best-of-seven playoff series after trailing three games to none, coming back to beat the New York Yankees before going on to win the World Series for the first time in 86 years.

components.note: 车 (cart) — 轻 originally described a light, nimble cart, extended to 'light (weight), gentle.'
工 (gōng) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from qīng.
车 (cart) — 轻 originally described a light, nimble cart, extended to 'light (weight), gentle.'
工 (gōng) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from qīng.

example.hanzi: 她轻轻地关上了门。
example.pinyin: Tā qīngqīng de guānshàng le mén.
example.english: She gently closed the door.
example.fact: A whisper typically registers around 20-30 decibels, roughly a million times quieter in sound intensity than a jet engine at close range, which can exceed 140 decibels — the decibel scale is logarithmic, so each 10-decibel increase represents a tenfold jump in sound intensity.

components.note: 用 is thought to depict either a wooden bucket or a tortoise-shell/bone used in divination rituals; its original picture is debated, but it came to mean 'to use, to employ.'
口 (mouth), stacked three times — many mouths talking about or judging something, the source of 品's meaning 'product, item; quality, rank.'

example.hanzi: 这家商店专卖厨房用品。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā shāngdiàn zhuān mài chúfáng yòngpǐn.
example.english: This shop specializes in kitchen goods.
example.fact: The modern zipper was perfected in 1913 by Swedish-American engineer Gideon Sundback, who redesigned earlier fastening devices into the interlocking-tooth design still used today; it took decades longer, however, before the fashion industry widely adopted zippers in clothing.

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 账 relates to money and financial records.
长 (zhǎng) gives a sound close to zhàng, sharing the same rhyme and initial.
单 is a simplification of 單, thought to depict a forked hunting tool, possibly an early slingshot or trap; the original meaning faded as the character came to mean 'single, alone, simple.'

example.hanzi: 服务员把账单送到了桌上。
example.pinyin: Fúwùyuán bǎ zhàngdān sòng dào le zhuō shàng.
example.english: The waiter brought the bill to the table.
example.fact: Double-entry bookkeeping, the accounting method where every transaction is recorded as both a debit and a credit, was first systematically described in 1494 by Italian friar and mathematician Luca Pacioli, earning him the nickname 'the father of accounting' even though merchants in Venice and Genoa had been using informal versions of the practice for over a century.

components.note: 異 (yì) is close in sound to dài, forming the upper portion of the character.
戈 (a dagger-axe) sits at the base; 戴 originally related to carrying or raising something up, as on the head, and later came to mean 'to wear, to put on.'
纟 (thread/silk) — 维 relates to a connecting thread or fiber, extended to mean 'to maintain, to link'
隹 (zhuī) gives a loose sound connection to 维's reading wéi

example.hanzi: 戴维每天早上都去公园跑步。
example.pinyin: Dàiwéi měitiān zǎoshang dōu qù gōngyuán pǎobù.
example.english: David goes jogging in the park every morning.
example.fact: Michelangelo's marble statue of David, carved between 1501 and 1504 from a single block of Carrara marble that other sculptors had abandoned as flawed, stands over 5.17 meters tall and is displayed today in the Galleria dell'Accademia in Florence, Italy.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — held in a hand, the image behind 布's meaning 'cloth' and, by extension, 'to spread out, distribute.'
鱼 (fish) forms the top of the character.
日, placed beneath the fish, was linked to the idea of speaking crudely or bluntly, giving 鲁 its meaning 'rash, uncouth.'
其 (qí) is close in sound to sī, forming the left side of the character.
斤 (an axe) originally tied 斯 to the meaning 'to split, to tear apart'; the character was later borrowed for its sound to serve as a grammatical particle and in transliterations.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢在酒吧里弹布鲁斯音乐。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zài jiǔbā lǐ tán bùlǔsī yīnyuè.
example.english: He likes to play blues music in the bar.
example.fact: Blues music originated in the Deep South of the United States in the late 19th century, growing out of African American spirituals, work songs, and field hollers, and its distinctive 'blue notes' — pitches bent slightly flat between the standard notes of a Western scale — went on to shape jazz, rock and roll, and much of the popular music that followed.

components.note: 又 (a hand) — reaching to take hold of something.
耳 (ear) — from an ancient battlefield practice of taking a fallen enemy's ear as proof of a kill, the origin of 取's meaning 'to take, obtain.'
夭 (a person leaning back) — the pose of someone laughing.
⺮ (bamboo-like strokes) — suggesting a wide grin, giving 笑 its meaning 'to laugh, smile.'

example.hanzi: 别取笑他了,他已经很难过了。
example.pinyin: Bié qǔxiào tā le, tā yǐjīng hěn nánguò le.
example.english: Stop teasing him, he's already very upset.
example.fact: Laughter is remarkably contagious and largely involuntary: research on human vocalizations has found that people are far more likely to laugh in a social setting with others than when alone, even when the content isn't especially funny, suggesting laughter evolved partly as a social bonding signal rather than purely a response to humor.

components.note: 缶 (jar/pottery) — 罐 names a type of container, a jar or pot.
雚 (guàn) gives the sound — an exact match with 罐.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 妈妈把糖果放进了一个玻璃罐子里。
example.pinyin: Māma bǎ tángguǒ fàng jìn le yí gè bōli guànzi lǐ.
example.english: Mom put the candy into a glass jar.
example.fact: Glassmaking dates back at least 3,600 years to ancient Mesopotamia and Egypt, but it was the Romans who, around the 1st century BC, developed glassblowing — a technique that made producing hollow vessels like jars and bottles dramatically faster and helped spread glass containers throughout the ancient world.

components.note: 囗 (an enclosure) — 四 pictures a bounded space.
儿 (a person) — a person enclosed within four walls gave 四 its meaning 'four,' though the exact link to the number is debated.
冂 depicts a boundary or border enclosing an area.
土 (earth/land) — the land enclosed within the border.
口 here depicts a well within that land — together giving 周 its early meaning of a bounded territory, and later 'circumference, week, the Zhou dynasty.'

example.hanzi: 四周一片寂静,只能听到风声。
example.pinyin: Sìzhōu yī piàn jìjìng, zhǐ néng tīngdào fēngshēng.
example.english: Everything around was silent; only the sound of the wind could be heard.
example.fact: The Orfield Labs anechoic chamber in Minneapolis, certified by Guinness World Records as the quietest place on Earth, absorbs 99.99% of sound and measures background noise at negative 20.6 decibels — so silent that visitors reportedly begin to hear their own heartbeat and blood flow after just a few minutes inside.

components.note: 王 (jade, written as the radical for 玉) — 珍 names something precious, like a valuable jewel.
彡 (shān) gives a sound distantly related to zhēn, having drifted apart over time.
贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 贵 relates to worth and cost.

example.hanzi: 这份手稿是极其珍贵的历史文物。
example.pinyin: Zhè fèn shǒugǎo shì jíqí zhēnguì de lìshǐ wénwù.
example.english: This manuscript is an extremely precious historical artifact.
example.fact: The Codex Sinaiticus, one of the oldest surviving copies of the Christian Bible, was written in Greek around the 4th century AD and rediscovered in fragments at Saint Catherine's Monastery in the Sinai Desert in the 19th century; its remaining pages are now digitized and split among libraries in the UK, Germany, Russia, and Egypt.

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
寸 (a hand) reaching for 旦 (originally 貝, a shell used as currency) — a picture of grasping something valuable, hence 'to obtain, to get.'

example.hanzi: 未经允许,不得进入此区域。
example.pinyin: Wèi jīng yǔnxǔ, bù dé jìnrù cǐ qūyù.
example.english: Without permission, you must not enter this area.
example.fact: Area 51, a highly classified United States Air Force facility in the Nevada desert, was not officially acknowledged by the U.S. government to even exist by that name until a 2013 CIA document declassification confirmed it, decades after it became a fixture of American pop culture and UFO folklore.

components.note: 大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.
皿 (dish, vessel) — 盔 (a helmet) is a rounded, bowl-like vessel worn on the head.
灰 (huī) gives a sound distantly related to kuī, sharing the same final but having drifted apart in initial consonant over time.

example.hanzi: 骑摩托车一定要戴头盔。
example.pinyin: Qí mótuōchē yídìng yào dài tóukuī.
example.english: You must wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle.
example.fact: Studies by the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration have found that motorcycle helmets are about 37% effective in preventing rider deaths and 41% effective for passengers, and modern helmet standards trace back to designs developed after World War I to protect fighter pilots and dispatch riders from head injuries.

components.note: A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'
片 (a thin slice/board) — 牌 names a flat board or sign, like a nameplate.
卑 (bēi) gives a sound close to pái.

example.hanzi: 那辆车的车牌号码我记不清了。
example.pinyin: Nà liàng chē de chēpái hàomǎ wǒ jì bù qīng le.
example.english: I can't quite remember that car's license plate number.
example.fact: France introduced the world's first mandatory vehicle registration plates in 1893, requiring car owners to display a name and address plate; the practice spread quickly, and by the early 20th century most industrialized countries had adopted standardized license plate systems to track vehicle ownership.

components.note: An altered form of 囟 (the mind/head) — the seat of thought.
心 (heart) — thinking was pictured as an activity of both mind and heart, giving 思 its meaning 'to think.'
纟 (thread/silk) — 维 relates to a connecting thread or fiber, extended to mean 'to maintain, to link'
隹 (zhuī) gives a loose sound connection to 维's reading wéi

example.hanzi: 学习编程可以锻炼逻辑思维。
example.pinyin: Xuéxí biānchéng kěyǐ duànliàn luójí sīwéi.
example.english: Learning programming can train logical thinking.
example.fact: Nobel laureate Daniel Kahneman's research, later popularized in his book Thinking, Fast and Slow, described two systems of thought: a fast, intuitive 'System 1' and a slower, more deliberate 'System 2' — a framework that has become foundational in behavioral economics and decision-making research.

components.note: 邦 (a nation/state) — a community bound together
巾 (a flag/cloth) — a banner people rally around to support one another
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 他在厨房里是我的好帮手。
example.pinyin: Tā zài chúfáng lǐ shì wǒ de hǎo bāngshou.
example.english: He is my good helper in the kitchen.
example.fact: Guide dogs for the blind undergo roughly six months of specialized training after puppyhood, learning to navigate obstacles and stop at curbs, and even practice what trainers call 'intelligent disobedience' — refusing a command from their handler when it would lead them into danger, such as stepping into oncoming traffic.

components.note: 走 (to walk/run) — 起 relates to standing up and setting into motion.
己 (jǐ) gives a close sound cue — 起 is pronounced qǐ, sharing the same final sound.
立 depicts a person standing with arms and legs spread, on a horizontal line representing the ground — a simple picture of standing upright.

example.hanzi: 老师走进教室,同学们都起立问好。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī zǒu jìn jiàoshì, tóngxuémen dōu qǐlì wènhǎo.
example.english: When the teacher walked into the classroom, the students all stood up to greet her.
example.fact: Humans are among the few mammals that habitually stand fully upright on two legs, a posture called bipedalism that likely emerged in early hominins at least 4 million years ago; standing upright freed the hands for tool use but also concentrates body weight through the spine and hips in ways that make lower-back problems more common in humans than in most other animals.

components.note: 目 (eye) — 眼 refers directly to the eye itself.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound hint — 眼 is pronounced yǎn; the rhyme has drifted apart over the centuries.
A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'

example.hanzi: 在父母眼中,孩子永远是孩子。
example.pinyin: Zài fùmǔ yǎnzhōng, háizi yǒngyuǎn shì háizi.
example.english: In parents' eyes, children are always children.
example.fact: The human eye can distinguish around 10 million different colors, according to research on color perception, yet contains only three types of cone cells sensitive to red, green, and blue wavelengths of light — all perceived color arises from the brain combining signals from just these three receptor types.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'
辶 (to walk) — encountering someone often happens while moving or traveling.
禺 (yú) gives a sound close to yù, with the tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 他们在一次旅行中意外相遇。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài yī cì lǚxíng zhōng yìwài xiāngyù.
example.english: They unexpectedly met each other during a trip.
example.fact: Voyager 1, launched by NASA in 1977, used a rare gravitational alignment of Jupiter and Saturn to slingshot itself toward interstellar space; it is now the most distant human-made object from Earth, and its trajectory depended on a planetary arrangement that occurs only about once every 176 years.

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of currency) — 质 originally meant 'pledge, hostage,' something valuable given as a guarantee, extended to 'quality, substance, nature.'
十 (shí) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from zhì.
里 (a unit of distance, related to a village measure) — 量 relates to measuring quantity.
旦 (dàn) gives a hint of the sound — 量 is pronounced liàng, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 这台机器的质量非常好。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái jīqì de zhìliàng fēicháng hǎo.
example.english: This machine's quality is very good.
example.fact: The kilogram was redefined in 2019 by the International Bureau of Weights and Measures to be based on Planck's constant rather than a physical platinum-iridium cylinder kept in France since 1889 — the last of the seven SI base units to abandon a physical artifact in favor of a definition rooted in fundamental constants of nature.

components.note: 止 (a foot, stepping forward) — 先 pictures someone moving ahead of another.
儿 (a person) — one person stepping ahead of another gave 先 its meaning 'before' or 'first.'
辶 (to walk) — 进 relates to advancing or entering, both movement-related.
井 (jǐng) gives a close sound cue — 进 is pronounced jìn, sharing similar consonant and vowel sounds.

example.hanzi: 这家公司使用了非常先进的技术。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī shǐyòng le fēicháng xiānjìn de jìshù.
example.english: This company uses very advanced technology.
example.fact: The James Webb Space Telescope, launched in December 2021, unfolded a sunshield the size of a tennis court and a 6.5-meter gold-coated beryllium mirror after reaching its observation point nearly 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, at a location called the second Lagrange point where gravitational forces let it hold a stable position relative to the Earth and Sun.

components.note: 心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.
王 (a variant form of 玉, meaning jade) — 理 originally referred to the natural grain or pattern in jade, later extending to 'reason, logic, to manage.'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — 理 is also pronounced lǐ, an exact match.
冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.

example.hanzi: 她大学时主修心理学。
example.pinyin: Tā dàxué shí zhǔxiū xīnlǐxué.
example.english: She majored in psychology in college.
example.fact: Wilhelm Wundt opened the first laboratory dedicated exclusively to psychological research in Leipzig, Germany, in 1879, a milestone widely regarded as marking psychology's emergence as a distinct experimental science separate from philosophy.

components.note: 无 is a simplification of 無, originally a pictograph of a person dancing while holding decorated sleeves or tassels; the dance sense was later replaced by 舞, while 無/无 was borrowed to mean 'without, nothing.'
宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.
丁 (a stylized handle/hook shape in the ancient form) — part of the character's original picture, now mostly opaque in the modern form
口 (kǒu, mouth) gives a sound related to 可's pronunciation kě, and may connect to 可's sense of approval spoken aloud
彐 here depicts a broom, standing in for 帚 in the traditional form 歸 — the image of a wife returning home with her broom gave 归 its meaning 'to return.'

example.hanzi: 地震过后,许多人无家可归。
example.pinyin: Dìzhèn guòhòu, xǔduō rén wú jiā kě guī.
example.english: After the earthquake, many people were left homeless.
example.fact: The 1976 Tangshan earthquake in northern China, measuring around magnitude 7.8, struck a densely populated industrial city with little warning in the middle of the night and is estimated to have killed several hundred thousand people, making it one of the deadliest earthquakes of the 20th century.

components.note: 宀 (a roof) — a house where valuables are kept
玉 (jade) — the treasure kept safe inside
贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 贵 relates to worth and cost.

example.hanzi: 时间是最宝贵的财富。
example.pinyin: Shíjiān shì zuì bǎoguì de cáifù.
example.english: Time is the most valuable wealth.
example.fact: The most precise atomic clocks today, based on the vibrations of cesium or strontium atoms, are accurate to within one second over roughly 15 billion years — longer than the current age of the universe — and they underpin the GPS satellite network, where even nanosecond-level timing errors can translate into positioning errors of several meters.

components.note: 直 (straight, upright) — 真 relates to something level and true.
几 (a small table) — an object placed level and true on a table gave 真 its meaning 'real' or 'true.'
王 (a variant form of 玉, meaning jade) — 理 originally referred to the natural grain or pattern in jade, later extending to 'reason, logic, to manage.'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — 理 is also pronounced lǐ, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 科学家们不断探索自然界的真理。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiāmen bùduàn tànsuǒ zìránjiè de zhēnlǐ.
example.english: Scientists continuously explore the truths of the natural world.
example.fact: Galileo Galilei's telescopic observations of Jupiter's four largest moons in 1610 provided some of the earliest direct evidence against the geocentric model of the universe, since the moons clearly orbited Jupiter rather than Earth — a finding that put him in direct conflict with church doctrine and eventually led to his trial by the Roman Inquisition in 1633.

components.note: 市's ancient form has been linked to a flag or banner raised over a marketplace, signaling a place open for trade — the origin of its meaning 'market, city, municipality.'
A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'
心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.

example.hanzi: 我们的办公室在市中心。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen de bàngōngshì zài shìzhōngxīn.
example.english: Our office is downtown.
example.fact: Manhattan's street grid, laid out by the Commissioners' Plan of 1811, imposed a rigid pattern of numbered streets and avenues across most of the island well before the city grew to fill it, a rare example of urban planning that anticipated growth decades ahead of the population it would eventually serve.

components.note: Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'
亻 (person) — a person's spoken word.
言 (speech, words) — together, a person standing by their word gave 信 its meaning 'trust, faith,' and later 'letter, message.'

example.hanzi: 我今天收到了一封来信。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān shōudào le yī fēng láixìn.
example.english: I received a letter today.
example.fact: The Pony Express, which operated for only about 18 months in 1860-1861, used relays of horseback riders to carry mail nearly 3,200 kilometers between Missouri and California in about 10 days — a dramatic improvement over previous overland routes that became obsolete almost overnight once the transcontinental telegraph was completed.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 级 originally named a strand or rank of silk thread, extended to 'grade, level, rank.'
及 (jí) gives the sound — 级 is also pronounced jí, an exact match.
另 (other, separate) — 别 relates to distinguishing one thing from another.
刂 (knife) — cutting things apart to sort them gave 别 its meaning 'to separate' or 'other,' and later, 'don't' as a command.

example.hanzi: 这次考试分成不同的级别。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì fēnchéng bùtóng de jíbié.
example.english: This exam is divided into different levels.
example.fact: The Japanese martial art of judo introduced the now widespread colored-belt ranking system in the late 19th century under founder Jigoro Kano, originally using just white and black belts to mark beginner and advanced practitioners before later schools expanded it into the multi-color system familiar today.

components.note: 马 (simplified from 馬) depicts a horse in profile, with its mane, legs, and tail visible — later simplified into just a few strokes.
足 (foot) — relates to 路's meaning 'road, path,' something walked on with feet.
各 (gè) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from lù.

example.hanzi: 过马路的时候要看红绿灯。
example.pinyin: Guò mǎlù de shíhou yào kàn hónglǜdēng.
example.english: You should watch the traffic lights when crossing the street.
example.fact: The world's first electric traffic signal was installed in Cleveland, Ohio, in 1914, using red and green lights controlled manually from a booth; the now-familiar three-color signal with a separate yellow caution light wasn't patented until 1923, by inventor Garrett Morgan.

components.note: 立 (to stand) pictures a person standing firm.
兄 (elder brother, here a rival) suggests standing up against someone, giving 竞 its meaning 'to compete, to contend.'
贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 赛 originally related to offering valuables, later coming to mean 'to compete.'
宀 (mián) gives a sound distantly related to sài, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他在数学竞赛中获得了第一名。
example.pinyin: Tā zài shùxué jìngsài zhōng huòdé le dì yī míng.
example.english: He won first place in the math competition.
example.fact: The International Mathematical Olympiad, first held in Romania in 1959 with just seven participating countries, has grown into the world's largest and most prestigious math competition for pre-university students, now drawing well over 100 countries each year and often serving as an early proving ground for future Fields Medal winners.

components.note: 三 is made of three simple horizontal strokes stacked together — the most direct way to picture the number three, following the same pattern as 一 (one) and 二 (two).
灬 (fire) — 点 originally related to a small flame or dot of light, giving rise to the meaning 'dot' or 'point.'
占 (zhàn) gives a hint of the sound — 点 is pronounced diǎn, a connection that has drifted over the centuries.

example.hanzi: 会议将在下午三点开始。
example.pinyin: Huìyì jiāng zài xiàwǔ sān diǎn kāishǐ.
example.english: The meeting will start at three o'clock in the afternoon.
example.fact: Mechanical clocks with escapements — the mechanism that regulates a clock's ticking speed — first appeared in European monasteries around the late 13th century, built primarily to ensure monks woke for prayers at precise hours, well before clock faces with hour hands became common on public buildings.

meanings: it had not occurred to me

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 想 relates to thinking, missing someone, or wanting something in one's heart.
相 (xiāng) gives the sound — 想 is pronounced xiǎng, matching aside from tone.
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
至 (zhì, to arrive) — carries 到's core meaning, 'to reach, to arrive'
刂 (a form of 刀, dāo) gives a sound close to 到's pronunciation dào

example.hanzi: 真想不到你会来参加这次聚会。
example.pinyin: Zhēn xiǎngbudào nǐ huì lái cānjiā zhè cì jùhuì.
example.english: I really didn't expect you to come to this gathering.
example.fact: Penicillin was discovered by accident in 1928 when Scottish scientist Alexander Fleming noticed that a mold, Penicillium notatum, had contaminated one of his bacterial culture plates and was killing the surrounding bacteria — an observation from a messy lab that led directly to the development of the first widely used antibiotic.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.
日 (the sun) — sunlight falling over the land
京 (a capital city) — a grand city view worth seeing

example.hanzi: 那个感人的情景让我至今难忘。
example.pinyin: Nàge gǎnrén de qíngjǐng ràng wǒ zhìjīn nánwàng.
example.english: That touching scene remains unforgettable to me even now.
example.fact: Psychologists use the term 'flashbulb memory' to describe the vivid, detailed recollections people often report for the moment they learned of a major shocking event — though research since the term was coined in 1977 has shown these memories, however vivid they feel, are not actually more accurate than ordinary memories and can shift substantially over time.

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 赛 originally related to offering valuables, later coming to mean 'to compete.'
宀 (mián) gives a sound distantly related to sài, having drifted apart over time.
禾 (a grain stalk) — a crop ready for harvest.
子 here representing a seed, together giving 季 its meaning 'season,' the time for planting and harvest.

example.hanzi: 这支球队在新赛季表现出色。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī qiúduì zài xīn sàijì biǎoxiàn chūsè.
example.english: This team has performed excellently in the new season.
example.fact: The NBA's regular season expanded from a shorter schedule when the league formed in 1946 to the modern 82-game format adopted in the 1967-68 season, a schedule length that has remained essentially unchanged for more than five decades despite ongoing debate about player fatigue and injury risk.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 察 relates to careful observation
祭 (jì) gives a loose sound connection to 察's reading chá
见 (to see, perceive) — relates to 觉's meaning 'to feel, sense, perceive.'
⺍ is a small graphic element serving as the phonetic hint, though its link to jué's modern sound has faded after centuries of change.

example.hanzi: 她察觉到了空气中的一丝异味。
example.pinyin: Tā chájué dào le kōngqì zhōng de yī sī yìwèi.
example.english: She sensed a faint strange smell in the air.
example.fact: The human nose can distinguish more than one trillion different odors, according to a 2014 study published in Science, a figure far higher than the previously assumed range of about 10,000 — overturning decades of textbook estimates about the limits of human smell.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — relates directly to 病's meaning 'illness, disease, to be sick.'
丙 (bǐng) gives a sound hint — 病 is pronounced bìng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 医生每天都会检查病人的病情。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng měitiān dōu huì jiǎnchá bìngrén de bìngqíng.
example.english: The doctor checks the patient's condition every day.
example.fact: Florence Nightingale, working as a nurse during the Crimean War in the 1850s, pioneered the systematic use of statistics in medicine, using data visualizations she called 'coxcomb' diagrams to show that far more soldiers were dying from preventable diseases in unsanitary hospitals than from battlefield wounds — work that helped drive major reforms in hospital hygiene.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 概 originally referred to a wooden leveling bar used to strike excess grain off a measure, later extended to 'in general, roughly'
既 (jì) gives a sound distantly related to 概's reading gài, having drifted apart over time
今 (now, the present) — represents what is currently on one's mind.
心 (heart/mind) — keeping the present moment in mind gave 念 its meaning 'to think of, to read aloud, to study.'

example.hanzi: 这是一个很难理解的抽象概念。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yī gè hěn nán lǐjiě de chōuxiàng gàiniàn.
example.english: This is an abstract concept that's very difficult to understand.
example.fact: The concept of zero as a number in its own right, rather than merely a placeholder, was formally developed in India, with the mathematician Brahmagupta providing rules for arithmetic with zero around 628 AD — a conceptual leap that took centuries longer to be adopted in Europe, where Roman numerals had no symbol for zero at all.

components.note: 龶 depicts a poisonous plant, tying 毒 to its meaning 'poison.'
母 (mǔ) gives a rhyme close to dú, with the initial shifted.
艹 (grass/plant) — many traditional medicines were made from plants and herbs
约 (yuē) gives a sound related to 药's reading yào, from an older, closer pronunciation link

example.hanzi: 那部小说的凶手用毒药害死了受害者。
example.pinyin: Nà bù xiǎoshuō de xiōngshǒu yòng dúyào hàisǐ le shòuhàizhě.
example.english: The murderer in that novel killed the victim using poison.
example.fact: The 16th-century physician Paracelsus is credited with founding modern toxicology through his principle that 'the dose makes the poison' — meaning virtually any substance, even water or oxygen, can become toxic at a high enough dose, while many well-known poisons are harmless or even beneficial in small enough quantities.
